rot.overload.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side, with Black to move. This position comes from a game played on Lichess.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.e2: The black queen on f3 attacks the white queen on d5, but the rook on d1 defends it. The same rook also guards e1, where the black rook would give check.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.p: Find the move that forces the rook on d1 to give up the defence of the queen.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.certo: The rook gives check on e1, and White's only reply is to capture it with the rook on d1.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the rook check on e1: White can only capture the rook with the rook on d1.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.err.f3d5.1: The queen captures the queen on d5, but the rook on d1 defends it.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.err.f3d5.2: With this move White recaptures with the rook, and the queens are simply traded: the game is level.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.err.f3d5.3: Back to the position: look for a move that takes the rook on d1 away from the defence of the queen.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.err.h6e3.1: The bishop goes to e3, but the queen on f3 is still attacked by the queen on d5.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.err.h6e3.2: With this move White has a resource: the white queen captures the black queen, which was undefended.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.err.h6e3.3: Back to the position: the queens attack each other. Look for a move with tempo that takes the rook on d1 away from the defence of the queen.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.err.f3e2.1: The queen leaves f3 and stops attacking the queen on d5.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.err.f3e2.2: With this move White has a resource: the queen leaves d5 and attacks the rook on e8 and the pawn on f6. The overload is gone, and White stays a knight up.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.err.f3e2.3: Back to the position: while the rook on d1 defends the queen, look for the move that gives it a second duty.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not take the rook on d1 away from the defence of the queen. Look for a check that only that rook can answer.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the check.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.l1: With the check, White must answer before anything else. The king has no free square, and no piece can step between the rook and the king.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.l2: So the rook on d1 captures on e1 and leaves the d-file. The queen on d5 is left undefended.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.l3: The black queen captures the white queen. Black gave up a rook and won the queen.
rot.overload.ideia.ex1.l4: This is overload: one piece with two duties, here defending the queen and guarding e1. In positions like this, a move with tempo, such as a check, forces the piece to fulfil one duty, and the other is left undefended.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: another position from a Lichess game, again with Black, who are a bishop down. The black queen on g5 attacks the white queen on d5.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.e2: The bishop on g2 has two duties: it defends the queen on d5 and the pawn on h3, which shields the king.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.p: Find the move that forces the bishop to choose between its two duties.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.certo: The rook captures the pawn on h3 with check. If the bishop recaptures, the queen on d5 is left undefended.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is the rook capture on h3, with check: the bishop on g2 must decide what it defends.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.err.g5d5.1: The queen captures the queen on d5, but the bishop on g2 defends it.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.err.g5d5.2: With this move White has a resource: the bishop recaptures on d5, the queens are traded, and Black is still a bishop down.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.err.g5d5.3: Back to the position: look for a move with tempo that gives the bishop on g2 work to do.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.err.g5g3.1: The queen goes to g3 and stops attacking the queen on d5.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.err.g5g3.2: With this move White has a resource: the rook goes to f1 and, together with the queen, attacks the pawn on f7. Black is still a bishop down.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.err.g5g3.3: Back to the position: while the queens attack each other, look for the move with tempo that gives the bishop on g2 work to do.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.err.g5h4.1: The queen goes to h4 and stops attacking the queen on d5.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.err.g5h4.2: With this move White has a resource: the rook goes to f1 and, together with the queen, attacks the pawn on f7. Black is still a bishop down.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.err.g5h4.3: Back to the position: while the queens attack each other, look for the move with tempo that gives the bishop on g2 work to do.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.err.e3e2.1: The rook leaves e3, but the queen on g5 is still attacked by the queen on d5.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.err.e3e2.2: With this move White has a resource: the white queen captures the black queen, which was undefended.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.err.e3e2.3: Back to the position: look for a move with tempo that gives the bishop on g2 work to do.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not force the bishop on g2 away from the defence of the queen. Look for a capture with check.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: look for the capture with check.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.l1: The check comes with a capture: the bishop cannot recapture on h3 and keep defending the queen.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.l2: The bishop recaptures the rook, which was attacking the king, and leaves the diagonal that defended the queen. If the king went to g1, the black queen would give check on e3, and the attack would go on.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.l3: The black queen captures the white queen with check.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.l4: The bishop returns to g2 and blocks the check. Black gave up a rook and won the queen.
rot.overload.ideia.ex2.l5: In positions like this, before attacking a defended piece, see whether the defender has another duty. Here the bishop could not defend the pawn and the queen at the same time.
rot.overload.demos.semXeque.1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side, in a position from a Lichess game. The black queen on b3 attacks the rook on c2, which the white queen on d3 defends. The same queen also defends the pawn on e3.
rot.overload.demos.semXeque.2: The knight captures the pawn on e3, without check. Now it attacks both white rooks, on d1 and on c2.
rot.overload.demos.semXeque.3: The white queen recaptures the knight. By going to e3, it gives up the defence of the rook on c2.
rot.overload.demos.semXeque.4: The black queen captures the rook on c2. There was no check here: the capture on e3 threatened the rooks, and that was enough to force the white queen to choose.
rot.overload.demos.cavaloXeque.1: Attack: Black again, in another Lichess game. The black queen on d8 attacks the white queen on d3, which the rook on d1 defends. The same rook guards the square e1.
rot.overload.demos.cavaloXeque.2: The knight gives check on e1 and also attacks the queen on d3: it is a fork. If the king steps out of check, the knight captures the queen.
rot.overload.demos.cavaloXeque.3: So the rook on d1 captures the knight. It leaves the d-file, and the queen on d3 is left undefended.
rot.overload.demos.cavaloXeque.4: The black queen captures the white queen. Black gave up the knight and won the queen: the fork gave the rook a second duty.
rot.overload.demos.xequeDama.1: Attack: back to White, in a position from a Lichess game. The white queen on h6 attacks the bishop on e6, defended only by the black queen on e5. See what other duty that queen can be given.
rot.overload.demos.xequeDama.2: The queen gives check on g6, along the g-file. The only piece that can block the check is the queen on e5, on g7.
rot.overload.demos.xequeDama.3: Black blocks the check with the queen, because with the king on h8 the rook on f2 would mate on h2. Now the bishop on e6 is undefended.
rot.overload.demos.xequeDama.4: The white queen captures the bishop on e6 with check.
rot.overload.demos.xequeDama.5: The rook on f8 blocks the check on f7. The black queen could not protect both the king and the bishop, and White won the bishop.
rot.overload.demos.excecao.1: Attack: still with Black. This position was set up from the first example: the white bishop left h2 and stands on b4. It looks like the same overload. Does it work here?
rot.overload.demos.excecao.2: The rook gives the same check on e1 as in the first position.
rot.overload.demos.excecao.3: The bishop on b4 captures the rook on e1. The rook on d1 did not have to move, the queen on d5 is still defended, and Black has simply lost the rook.
rot.overload.demos.excecao.4: Back to the position: before the overloading move, check whether another piece covers the same point. Here the bishop guarded e1, and the rook on d1 had only one duty.
rot.overload.demos.excecao.5: Without the overload, the soundest option is the queen trade: the black queen captures on d5.
rot.overload.demos.excecao.6: The rook recaptures, and the game is level. In positions like this, the pattern looks the same, but one piece on another square changes the evaluation.
rot.overload.pratica.valeAqui.enunciado: Your queen attacks the rook on b4, defended by the pawn on c3 and the knight on d5. Capturing on d4 would pull the pawn on c3 away. Does it work here? Play as Black.
rot.overload.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The capture on d4 did not work: the knight on d5 would still defend the rook. The knight was the piece with two duties, the pawn on c3 and the rook on b4. By recapturing on c3 it let go of the rook, and the queen captured it.
rot.overload.pratica.valeAqui.err.g7d4: The pawn on c3 recaptures the bishop, but the knight on d5 still defends the rook on b4, and you gave up the bishop for a pawn. Look for the defender that has two duties.
rot.overload.pratica.valeAqui.err.d6b4: The rook on b4 is defended: the pawn on c3 recaptures, and you give up the queen for a rook.
rot.overload.pratica.valeAqui.err.a7a5: The pawn goes to a5, but the rook on b4 captures the knight on a4, and White stays ahead in material. Look for the defender that has two duties.
rot.overload.pratica.valeAqui.err.b6b5: The pawn on b5 defends the knight on a4, but the rook on b4 captures the pawn, and White stays ahead in material. Look for the defender that has two duties.
rot.overload.pratica.valeAqui.err2.g7d4: The bishop captures the pawn on d4, but the rook on b4 escapes by capturing the pawn on c4, and you miss the chance to win the rook.
rot.overload.pratica.xequeTorre.enunciad: Back to White. Your queen on a3 attacks the black queen on d6, which the rook on d8 defends. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.overload.pratica.xequeTorre.fim: The rook on d8 defended the queen and the square c8. With the check on c8 it had to capture your rook, and the queen on d6 was left undefended.
rot.overload.pratica.xequeTorre.err.a3d6: The queen trade wins nothing: the rook on d8 recaptures. First look for a move that gives the rook on d8 another duty.
rot.overload.pratica.xequeTorre.err.e6d5: The bishop captures the knight on d5, but Black trades queens on a3, and the rook on d8 recaptures the bishop: you win nothing.
rot.overload.pratica.xequeTorre.err2.e6c: The bishop recaptures the rook, but Black trades queens on a3 and then captures the bishop on c8: you end up a piece down. First capture the queen on d6, which was left undefended.
rot.overload.pratica.mate.enunciado: Your rook on c1 attacks the rook on c8, which the queen on d8 defends. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.overload.pratica.mate.fim: The queen on d8 defended the rook on c8 and blocked the check on e7. From e7 it cannot go back to d8, because that would leave the king in check from the queen on e6: the capture on c8 was mate.
rot.overload.pratica.mate.err.c1c8: The rook trade wins nothing: the queen on d8 recaptures. Look for a check that only the queen on d8 can block.
rot.overload.pratica.mate.err.d4e5: The pawn captures the bishop, but Black trades rooks on c1 with check, and the attack on the rook on c8 is gone. Look for a check that only the queen on d8 can block.
rot.overload.pratica.mate.err2.e6e7: The queen captures the queen on e7, but the king recaptures, and the rook on f8 now defends the rook on c8. Capture the rook on c8 now, while it is undefended.
